doc.title: Artie Shaw — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Early years: Cleveland, Aaronson, New York
title: The Wingy Manone record session with Jelly Roll Morton and Bud Freeman
summary: Shaw recalls a chaotic unreleased date: Wingy sang the themes, Jelly Roll did his own thing, and later a tape surfaced; Venuti's cufflink joke.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Just before we get into the band starting, there’s one record session that you made which has always intrigued me. It’s just a small group, which had . . .
The one with Wingy Manone?
Wingy Manone, with Jelly Roll Morton on piano.
Yeah, and Chick I think was on drums? [No. Kaiser Marshall was on drums]
Yeah.
I’m not sure. I know he was on one session. And Bud [Freeman] and I.
And Frank Victor.
I don’t remember. It was never released until much later.
Right. It’s recently released.

Wingy went up to Harlem the night before, sat down with some arranger, and sang the themes to him. Then we got to the date. He couldn’t read, so he didn’t remember what he’d written. It was a mess of a date.
It’s quite amusing, though. How did Jelly Roll Morton happen to be on it?
Wingy was Wingy. He was weird. Wingy would find people. He dug up people.
It was one of the most extraordinary . . .
It was a strange date.
. . . extraordinary lineups in the history of jazz.
Yeah. Jelly didn’t fit in with that.
No.
He’s an individual.
[laughs] He did his own thing on it.

I know. It’s a strange record date. Nobody released it, because it was deemed, and probably correctly so, commercially unfeasible. But somebody to my amusement sent me a tape of it many years later. “I got Artie Shaw. I got Bud Freeman.”
That’s right.
He’s talking on the record, talking about who’s on the band. Yeah, Wingy was a character.
That’s right. Look at all the boys I’ve got with me today.
Joe Venuti once sent him a Christmas present: one cufflink. [laughter (Wingy had only one arm.)] And then the following year he sent him another cufflink, the same link. The other.
